title: Treated with suspicion
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on the acute medical unit. Mr Hall, 52, a Gypsy man who lives in a caravan, was admitted with cellulitis needing intravenous antibiotics.

He tells you staff keep checking his belongings and asking whether he has "taken anything". He says he feels treated like a criminal and wants to leave.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Explain why his antibiotics matter and encourage him to stay.
options.brief: He needs to understand the risks of leaving.
options.detailed: Cellulitis needing intravenous antibiotics can become serious. Explaining this may help him decide to stay. It ranks second.

options.text: Apologise, and listen to his experience.
options.detailed: Being treated with suspicion is upsetting and may reflect prejudice. An apology and listening may help him feel respected. It ranks first.

options.text: Tell him staff are just being careful.
options.detailed: This may confirm his sense of being treated unfairly.

options.text: Raise the staff's behaviour with the nurse in charge.
options.detailed: If he is being treated differently because of his background, it needs addressing. It ranks third because his immediate care comes first.

options.text: Tell him he is free to leave if he is unhappy.
options.brief: Accepts him leaving without addressing his concerns or the risks.
options.detailed: He has the right to leave, but this ignores the reason he wants to and the risks. It is the least appropriate option.

explanation.issue: This tests how you respond when a patient from a minority community feels discriminated against.
explanation.keyDetails: He feels treated like a criminal. He needs IV antibiotics. He wants to leave.
explanation.reasoning: [B] apologises and listens, [A] explains the risks, and [D] addresses staff behaviour. [C] dismisses him, and [E] lets him leave without addressing the cause.
explanation.competing: [A] and [D] are close. The key puts his treatment first because leaving could harm him.

references.title: Equality Act 2010
references.note: Race, including Gypsy and Traveller communities, as a protected characteristic.
